title: The Shepherd's Care and Peter's Duty
english: For this very thing was foretold even before the denial (John 21:15-17), showing indeed that he will be tested by the devil when he turns away from the confession into Christ, but by the help from Him, he remains upon the faith.

And it is necessary for the one receiving this help to show similar sparing and care toward the brothers. For 'Simon,' He says, 'Simon, behold, Satan has asked you to sift you like wheat (Luke 22:31). But I have prayed for you, so that your faith may not fail. And you, when you have turned back, strengthen your brothers' (Luke 22:32).'

The Lord repeats those words and says that, if you love the Teacher and Savior who kept you even until now in love, you must imitate my care toward you, strengthening the brothers and feeding them just as a shepherd feeds a flock, calling the sheep his own.

title: The Third Question and the Triple Confession of Love
english: Regarding the third of those questions, he is simultaneously making an exhortation to him that reminds him; at the same time, he is reminding him of the third denial having occurred, and opposing the triple confession of love against the triple denial and demanding the readiness of service, so that he might confess Christ in works, whom he denied by words while taking care of his own salvation (John 21:18-19).

He says that he will make an even greater proof of love through martyrdom, and prepares him to have this readiness, so that, opposing need with courage, he might remove the martyrdom unto death concerning the Lord, which previously had become a denial through fear of death.

title: The free transition and the promise of life
english: A free transition is held from the prisons of Hades because the soul is being led up to Christ. Therefore also the 'better to loose' is said by Paul, because of 'being with Christ' (Phil 1:23).

Thus, therefore, the word of the Lord was about those who in the end do not die. And this was made manifest by saying: 'He who believes in me, even if he dies, shall live, and everyone living and believing in me shall not die for ever' (John 11:25-26).

Because of this, they were making it without hopelessness to live and not to die. But it was laid up for those left behind until the presence of Christ, for those being born in the last generation, just as Paul taught.
And John points out that he himself did not have the promise of not dying, but the brothers, hearing this word, took this from ignorance (John 21:23).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
